span.label: The core metabolic networks of 43 organisms across archaea, bacteria and eukaryota, as drawn from the WIT pathway-genome database.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Is the topology of a metabolic network the homogeneous random kind predicted by Erdos-Renyi, or the heterogeneous scale-free kind found in the web and in social networks?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Shows that metabolic networks in all three domains of life are scale-free, and that their diameter is conserved across organisms of very different complexity - a property the non-biological scale-free networks do not have.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.term: growth with preferential attachment: new nodes join by attaching to already well connected ones, which is what produces the power law
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: hub dominance: a few highly connected substrates carry the connectivity, so removing them raises the diameter sharply and breaks the network into isolated clusters
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: error tolerance: because most substrates are sparsely connected, removing random ones leaves the average distance unchanged
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: increasing per-substrate connectivity is what holds the diameter constant as organisms get more complex
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Eighteen of the 43 organisms are not fully sequenced and many ORFs are functionally unassigned, so the substrate and reaction lists analysed are incomplete.
span.note: what this limits: the substrate and reaction lists every topology statistic is computed over: 18 OF THE 43 ORGANISMS ... ARE NOT YET FULLY SEQUENCED, AND A SUBSTANTIAL PORTION OF THE IDENTIFIED ORFs ARE FUNCTIONALLY UNASSIGNED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The extension of the conclusion to non-metabolic cellular networks is only preliminary, because those networks are too small for unambiguous statistical analysis with current tools.
span.note: what this limits: the extension beyond metabolism: OUR PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS SUGGEST[s] THAT CONNECTIVITY DISTRIBUTION OF NON-METABOLIC PATHWAYS ALSO FOLLOWS A POWER-LAW - preliminary, and by the authors' own account not statistically decidable
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: 18 of the 43 organisms were not fully sequenced and many ORFs are unassigned, so the substrate and reaction lists are known to be incomplete.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the enzyme list is incomplete by construction
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The generalisation to other cellular networks is explicitly not supported - those networks are too small for the statistics to be unambiguous.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with the reason: THE CURRENT MATHEMATICAL TOOLS DO NOT ALLOW UNAMBIGUOUS STATISTICAL ANALYSIS OF THE TOPOLOGY OF OTHER NETWORKS DUE TO THEIR RELATIVELY SMALL SIZE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The whole analysis rests on one predicted database, whose pathways are inferred from annotated genomes rather than observed.
span.note: what this limits: the object the whole analysis is about: THIS INTEGRATED PATHWAY-GENOME DATABASE PREDICTS THE EXISTENCE OF A GIVEN METABOLIC PATHWAY BASED ON THE ANNOTATED GENOME OF AN ORGANISM, so the network is inferred rather than measured
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across 43 organisms from all three domains of life, metabolic networks share the SAME scale-free topology (power-law degree distribution) as non-biological complex networks — a common blueprint dominated by a few highly connected hubs.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: This scale-free organization implies metabolic networks are robust and error-tolerant, following the same design principles as other scale-free networks.
span.note: about this quote: QUOTE REPAIRED (Q-697): the extractor split a hyphen-space and the quote was recorded faithfully with the damage in it, which made it unanchorable. The repaired string is an EXACT SUBSTRING of the staged text - that is why it was accepted, not because a rule produced it. The text as originally recorded is kept in `evidence_as_extracted`.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Metabolic networks in all three domains of life are scale-free: the number of reactions a substrate takes part in follows a power law.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The network diameter is the same in all 43 organisms regardless of how many substrates they have - which is not what network growth predicts, and the paper calls it unprecedented.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The identity of the hub substrates is essentially the same in every organism; species-specific differences appear only among the sparsely connected substrates.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The network survives random removal of substrates but not removal of its hubs - robust to error, fragile to attack.
